A patient asks for a zonulin blood test to prove that her rosacea comes from a leaky gut. What is the most accurate reply?
Explanation: Ask what a test measures before you ask what it shows.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): The test will show whether her gut barrier is causing the rosacea.
Explanation: A widely used zonulin assay detects other proteins, and a zonulin result cannot tell you what is causing her rosacea.
Correct answer: The test is unreliable and would not change care: treat the rosacea on its own evidence, and assess any gut symptoms clinically.
Explanation: Correct. The small trial that linked gut bacteria to rosacea used breath testing and clinical assessment, and no zonulin test.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Rosacea has nothing to do with the gut, so there is nothing to discuss.
Explanation: Too strong: a small randomized trial found rosace…

Closing Module 3: which statement keeps the four registers apart?
Explanation: One grade per outcome, one register per sentence.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Semaglutide ages the face by acting on facial fat, so the label should carry a facial warning.
Explanation: That blends an untested hypothesis with a regulatory conclusion. The labels list hair loss; a direct action on facial fat is untested in people.
Correct answer: Facial volume loss on incretins: fat loss deflates facial compartments (mechanism); small observational studies tie it to the amount of weight lost (human evidence); US labels list hair loss but not facial change (regulatory status); whether the drugs act directly on facial fat is untested (open question).

units.text:
Mechanism
A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.
GHK is a tripeptide found in human plasma, first described in 1973. Bound to copper it becomes GHK-Cu, which is proposed to deliver copper to enzymes such as superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and to switch on wound-healing and antioxidant gene programmes. Most of that mechanistic literature comes from the group that discovered the peptide.
Endogenous: GHK circulates in human plasma
Proposed: copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes
Mechanism register only — written largely by the originator
Narration: Start with the molecule. GHK is a three-amino-acid peptide that circulates in human plasma; it was first described in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex, GHK-Cu, is what skin-care labels mean when they say copper peptide. The proposed mechanism is that GHK-Cu delivers copper to enzymes that build and protect…

assertions.note: Pickart (2015) explicitly states that GHK is a tripeptide present in human plasma.

Since its discovery in 1973, GHK-Cu established itself as a powerful protective and regenerative ingredient, which is currently widely used in skin and hair products

units.text:
Human evidence
One indexed randomized trial.
A search of PubMed in September 2026 found one randomized controlled trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin: 2006, healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing. The cosmetic trials cited for anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed. Both Hormonaly guides grade topical use C.
1
indexed randomized trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin
Miller et al., 2006 — healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing, not photoageing
What it means: The human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small: one small indexed trial plus sponsor-run cosmetic studies. GRADE C is the honest ceiling.
What it does not mean: It does not show that GHK-Cu fails, that it treats photoageing, or anything about injecting it. A thin evidence base is an unknown, not a negative.
units.sourceNote: Miller 2006 · Peptide Pocket Guide · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology

Topical GHK-Cu
Collagen, skin repair · GRADE C small trials · Cat. 1
(topical)

units.text:
Four registers
Keep the four answers apart.
Every peptide question has four separate answers. For GHK-Cu they point in different directions, which is exactly why they must not be blended into one sentence.
Mechanism
Plausible
Copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes; gene-expression data from the originator
Human evidence
Topical: GRADE C · Injectable: none
One small indexed RCT and sponsor-run cosmetic trials; no randomized trials of injection
Regulatory status (US, 14 May 2026)
Non-injectable: 503A Category 1
Category 1 means FDA is still evaluating and does not intend to act against compounders who meet its conditions; an advisory-committee consultation is planned before the end of February 2027. The injectable route has no such standing.
Open question
Does it reach the dermis?
Penetration data are in vitro and depend on how they are measured
Callout: A strong mechanism is no…

assertions.text: The proposed mechanism of GHK-Cu involves copper delivery to extracellular matrix and antioxidant enzymes, supported by gene-expression data from the originator.
assertions.quote: This is very important since copper is required for more than a dozen vital enzymes in the human body and skin including those that participate in connective tissue formation, antioxidant defense, and cellular respiration.
assertions.note: Pickart (2015) describes GHK-Cu delivering copper to enzymes involved in connective tissue formation and antioxidant defense, as well as modulating gene expression.

assertions.text: Human clinical evidence for topical GHK-Cu is graded C, consisting of one small indexed RCT and sponsor-run cosmetic trials, while there are no randomized controlled trials of injectable GHK-Cu.
assertions.quote: Clinical caveat. Evidence base: topical cosmetic RCTs (cosmeceutical use) and preclinical wound-healing models — injectable human use rests on anecdote, no RCTs.
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni (2026 PPG) gives GHK-Cu GRADE C for topical cosmetic use and confirms injectable human use has no RCTs.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Serum yes, syringe no.
Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation at GRADE C. Injected GHK-Cu is a different product: no randomized trials, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the US the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing.
Topical: modest, small-trial support
Injectable: anecdote, common local reactions
Say which route you mean every time
Narration: Here is what that means in the room. Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation, as long as you describe the evidence honestly: small trials, modest effects, grade C. Injected GHK-Cu is not the same product in a stronger form. There are no randomized trials of injection, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the United States the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing that covers no…

units.text:
Lesson 4.2 · Concept
Three families, one question: who ran the trial?
Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are meant to tell fibroblasts to make matrix. SNAP-25 mimics (Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8) and Leuphasyl, an enkephalin analogue, are meant to quieten expression lines. Oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. All three families have a trial record, and in all three the question that matters most is who funded it.
Signal peptides: 'make more matrix'
SNAP-25 mimics: 'relax the line'
Oral collagen: the supplement aisle
Narration: Lesson two covers three families that fill the cosmetic and supplement shelves. Signal peptides, like palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, sold as Matrixyl, are fragments of matrix proteins meant to tell fibroblasts to make more collagen. SNAP-25 mimics, Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8, copy part of a nerve…
units.sourceNote: Lupo & Cole 2007 · Lintner & Peschard 2000 · Blanes-Mira 2002 · Errante 2020

assertions.text: Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are fragments of matrix proteins intended to signal fibroblasts to stimulate collagen and extracellular matrix synthesis.
assertions.quote: Matrixyl ® is the new version of Pentapeptide-4 (palmitoylated Lys-Thr-Thr-Lys-Ser-OH), the well-known signal peptide fragment of the C-terminal propeptide of type I collagen. It stimulates feedback regulation of new collagen synthesis and ECM proteins.
assertions.note: Errante 2020 describes Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4) as a fragment of the propeptide of type I collagen that stimulates new collagen and ECM synthesis.

assertions.text: SNAP-25 mimics such as Argireline and SNAP-8 emulate parts of the nerve-terminal protein targeted by botulinum neurotoxin to reduce muscle contraction and expression lines.
assertions.quote: One of the best known peptide with neurotransmitter-inhibiting properties is a synthetic hexapeptide, so-called acetyl hexapeptide-3 and coined Argireline . The sequence Ac-Glu-Glu-Met-Gln-Arg-Arg-NH 2 (Blanes-Mira et al., 2002 ), covers the N-terminal fragment domain of SNAP-25, promoting the inhibition of Ca 2+ -dependent catecholamine release through the interrupted formation of SNARE complex.
assertions.note: Errante 2020 confirms that Argireline covers the N-terminal domain of SNAP-25 and SNAP-8 mimics SNAP-25 to decrease muscle contraction.

assertions.text: Leuphasyl is an enkephalin analogue peptide used to reduce wrinkles and expression lines.
assertions.quote: Pentapeptide-18 ( Leuphasyl ) The pentapeptide-18 composed of the sequence H-Tyr-Ala-Gly-Phe-Leu-OH, was reported for the first time in 2015. It became one of the most popular active peptide ingredients in anti-aging formulations (Lipotec s.a., 2005 ). It acts like enkephalins, decreasing the ACh secretion in the synaptic cleft. Both instrumental and volunteer-involving studies acknowledge its effectiveness in wrinkles reduction (Dragomirescu et al., 2014 ).
assertions.note: Errante 2020 notes that Leuphasyl acts like enkephalins and reduces wrinkles.

assertions.text: Oral collagen peptides are consumed orally as dietary supplements and have a trial record that is predominantly small and industry funded.
assertions.quote: Oral collagen peptides show modest improvements in hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle parameters in randomized trials, though most are small and industry-funded GRADE C,[16] and topical GHK-Cu has decades of mechanistic and small-trial support for collagen stimulation GRADE C.[17]
assertions.note: Hannah-Shmouni 2026 notes that oral collagen peptides are backed by randomized trials that are mostly small and industry-funded.

units.text:
The evidence
Twenty-three trials, split by who paid.
Pooled, oral collagen trials show better hydration, elasticity and wrinkle scores, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades them C. A 2025 meta-analysis split the same kind of trials by funding and by quality. The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials. Unfunded and high-quality trials showed no effect.
23 RCTs
in the 2025 meta-analysis that split oral-collagen trials by funding and quality
1,474 participants
What it means: The pooled benefit of oral collagen disappears when you look only at independent or high-quality trials. The course keeps the guide's GRADE C and shows why a downgrade has been proposed to its author.
What it does not mean: It does not show collagen is harmful, and it does not rule out benefit for an individual. It is a statement about the evidence, and it says nothi…
units.sourceNote: Myung & Park, Am J Med 2025 · Pu 2023 · de Miranda 2021 · Kim 2018

assertions.text: Pooled oral collagen trials show improvements in skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle scores.
assertions.quote: In the meta-analysis, a grouped analysis of studies showed favorable results of hydrolyzed collagen supplementation compared with placebo in terms of skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles.
assertions.note: Supported by the pooled meta-analysis findings.

assertions.text: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide gives oral collagen peptides a GRADE C rating.
assertions.quote: Oral collagen peptides show modest improvements in hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle parameters in randomized trials, though most are small and industry-funded GRADE C,[16] and topical GHK-Cu has decades of mechanistic and small-trial support for collagen stimulation GRADE C.[17]
assertions.note: Supported by the guide's evidence rating.

assertions.text: A 2025 meta-analysis of 23 RCTs with 1,474 participants found that oral collagen benefits appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials, whereas non-industry-funded and high-quality trials showed no significant effect.
assertions.quote: A total of 23 RCTs with 1474 participants were analyzed. In a meta-analysis of all 23 RCTs, collagen supplements significantly improved skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles. However, in the subgroup meta-analysis by funding source, studies not receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies revealed no effect of collagen supplements for improving skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles, while those receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies did show significant effects. Similarly, high-quality studies revealed no significant effect in all categories, while low-quality studies revealed a significant improvement in elasticity.
assertions.note: Supported by the 2025 meta-analysis abstract.

units.text:
What changes in practice
Cosmetic, supplement, drug: three rulebooks.
In the US, cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework. Oral collagen is a dietary supplement: it may not claim to treat disease, and product quality and content vary. Neither route has to prove efficacy before sale — which is why the funding question matters.
Cosmetic ingredient: no efficacy approval needed
Dietary supplement: no disease claims; quality varies
Say 'modest, small-trial' — never 'topical Botox'
Narration: Now the regulatory register, stated for the United States. Cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs; their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework, and nobody has to prove they work before they are sold. Oral collagen is sold as a dietary supplement, so it cannot claim to treat a disease, and what is in the tub vari…
units.sourceNote: Bjerke 2026 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology · Pocket Guide

assertions.text: In the United States, cosmetic peptides are classified as cosmetic ingredients rather than drugs, subject to cosmetic safety frameworks without requiring premarket efficacy approval.
assertions.quote: Under the FD&C Act and the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act (MoCRA, 2022), a topical product that makes only appearance claims (moisturizing, improving the look of fine lines) is a cosmetic: no premarket approval, but safety and labeling rules apply.
assertions.note: MoCRA and FD&C Act regulatory framework for cosmetic topical peptides does not require premarket efficacy approval.

assertions.text: Oral collagen is marketed as a dietary supplement that cannot make disease treatment claims, and its product quality and content vary across brands.
assertions.quote: Sold as a supplement (e.g. oral collagen peptides); no disease claims · Discuss as a supplement; quality and dose vary.
assertions.note: Dietary supplements such as oral collagen peptides cannot claim disease treatment and have variable quality and dosage.

assertions.text: Cosmetic peptides should be framed as supported by modest, small-trial evidence rather than termed 'topical Botox'.
assertions.quote: Marketed as "topical botox" but the mechanism requires the peptide to reach the neuromuscular junction beneath facial muscles — most dermatology authorities consider this implausible at cosmetic concentrations. Cosmetic effect, if real, is modest and not a substitute for botulinum injections.
assertions.note: Cosmetic peptides marketed as 'topical botox' have modest effects and are not substitutes for botulinum toxin.

units.text: In the UK, a peptide serum is a cosmetic: its responsible person needs a safety assessment and must notify the regulator before sale, and must be able to prove its claims. Oral collagen is a food supplement: no food may claim to prevent, treat or cure disease, and only authorised health claims may be used. In May 2026 the UK advertising regulator ruled a peptide serum's 'clinically proven' lifting claim misleading because the study behind it was small and uncontrolled.

assertions.text: In the UK, a cosmetic's responsible person must ensure a safety assessment is completed, notify the regulator before making it available for sale, and be able to prove product claims.
assertions.quote: Before a cosmetic product is made available in GB, the Responsible Person must submit information on the cosmetic product to OPSS. This process is called notification.
assertions.note: UK cosmetics guidance states that the responsible person must have a product safety assessment, notify OPSS before making the product available, and substantiate marketing claims.

assertions.text: In the UK, food and food supplements cannot claim to prevent, treat, or cure human disease, and only authorised health claims may be used.
assertions.quote: In particular, any claim that a food has the property of preventing, treating or curing human disease is not permitted.
assertions.note: Food information and health claim regulations prohibit disease prevention, treatment, or cure claims and require health claims to be authorised.

assertions.text: In May 2026, the UK advertising regulator ruled a peptide serum's 'clinically proven' lifting claim misleading because the underlying study was small and lacked a control group.
assertions.quote: However, the study did not include a placebo or control group and only consisted of 30 subjects.
assertions.note: The ASA upheld the complaint against 111Skin in May 2026 because the 28-day trial had only 30 participants and no placebo or control group.

units.text: In the EU, a peptide serum sold as a cosmetic needs a responsible person in the EU, a safety assessment with a product safety report and electronic notification to the Commission before it is placed on the market (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009), and its claims must be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence (Regulation (EU) No 655/2013). Food labelling and advertising may not claim that a food prevents, treats or cures a disease, and health claims on foods are prohibited unless authorised: the Commission refused a claim that a collagen peptide mixture maintains skin health by increasing elasticity and reducing wrinkles, because cause and effect was not established (Regulation (EU) No 1154/2014), and the EU Register lists no authorised claim for collagen itself (searched 25 September 2026).

assertions.text: In the EU, a cosmetic product requires a responsible person, a safety assessment with a product safety report, and electronic notification to the Commission prior to being placed on the market (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009).
assertions.quote: In order to demonstrate that a cosmetic product complies with Article 3, the responsible person shall, prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, ensure that the cosmetic product has undergone a safety assessment on the basis of the relevant information and that a cosmetic product safety report is set up in accordance with Annex I.
assertions.note: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 mandates designating a responsible person, completing a safety assessment with a safety report, and electronically notifying the Commission before placing the product on the market.

assertions.text: Under Regulation (EU) No 655/2013, cosmetic claims must be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence.
assertions.quote: Claims for cosmetic products, whether explicit or implicit, shall be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence regardless of the types of evidential support used to substantiate them, including where appropriate expert assessments.
assertions.note: The regulation explicitly requires cosmetic claims to be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence.

assertions.text: Food labelling and advertising in the EU may not claim that a food prevents, treats, or cures a human disease (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011).
assertions.quote: Subject to derogations provided for by Union law applicable to natural mineral waters and foods for particular nutritional uses, food information shall not attribute to any food the property of preventing, treating or curing a human disease, nor refer to such properties.
assertions.note: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 prohibits attributing properties of preventing, treating, or curing a human disease to food information and advertising.

assertions.text: Health claims on foods in the EU are prohibited unless authorised.
assertions.quote: Health claims shall be prohibited unless they comply with the general requirements in Chapter II and the specific requirements in this Chapter and are authorised in accordance with this Regulation and included in the lists of authorised claims provided for in Articles 13 and 14.
assertions.note: Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006 prohibits health claims on food unless authorised and included in the Union lists.

assertions.text: The European Commission refused a health claim that a collagen peptide mixture maintains skin health by increasing elasticity and reducing wrinkles because a cause and effect relationship was not established (Regulation (EU) No 1154/2014).
assertions.quote: On 20 June 2013, the Commission and the Member States received the scientific opinion from the Authority, which concluded that on the basis of the data presented, a cause and effect relationship could not be established between the consumption of Verisol®P and the claimed effect. Accordingly, as the claim does not comply with the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006, it should not be authorised.
assertions.note: Regulation (EU) No 1154/2014 refused authorisation for the VeriSol P collagen peptide mixture claim after EFSA concluded cause and effect was not established.

units.text: In Portugal, INFARMED is the competent authority for cosmetics (Decreto-Lei 23/2025), and borderline products must be assessed case by case by the Responsible Person, taking all their characteristics into account (INFARMED, as of 25 September 2026). For food supplement notification, there is no evaluation of the product or validation of labelling; control is carried out afterwards by sampling and may take place at any time (DGAV, as of 25 September 2026).

units.text:
A patient shows you a collagen drink labelled 'clinically proven to reduce wrinkles'. What is the most accurate reply?
Explanation: Ask who paid for the trial before you ask what it showed.
Correct answer: The trials are real, but the benefit shows up only in industry-funded and lower-quality trials; independent, high-quality trials show no effect.
Explanation: Correct. That is what the 2025 funding-stratified meta-analysis found.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Meta-analyses prove that collagen improves skin.
Explanation: Pooled, yes. Split by funding and quality, the effect disappears in the independent and high-quality trials.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Collagen is digested, so it cannot do anything.
Explanation: That is a mechanism argument. The course rests on the trials, and the problem with the trials is who ran them.

assertions.text: In a 2025 meta-analysis, independent trials with no pharmaceutical funding showed no effect of collagen supplements on skin hydration, elasticity, or wrinkles, whereas industry-funded trials showed significant benefits.
assertions.quote: However, in the subgroup meta-analysis by funding source, studies not receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies revealed no effect of collagen supplements for improving skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles, while those receiving funding from pharmaceutical companies did show significant effects.
assertions.note: The 2025 meta-analysis found no significant effects in non-industry funded studies, while industry-funded studies showed significant effects.

assertions.text: High-quality trials showed no significant effect of collagen supplements across all skin aging categories, while benefits were found only in lower-quality trials.
assertions.quote: Similarly, high-quality studies revealed no significant effect in all categories, while low-quality studies revealed a significant improvement in elasticity.
assertions.note: High-quality studies showed no significant effects in any category, while low-quality trials showed significant improvement.

units.text:
Lesson 4.3 · Concept
Rodents, a fragment, and a tripeptide.
BPC-157 rests on a large rodent literature, mostly from one research group, and on uncontrolled human case series. TB-500 is not thymosin β4: it is a seven-residue fragment of it, identified by analysing the product itself, and no trial has tested the fragment. KPV, a tripeptide from the end of α-MSH, calms inflammation in mouse colitis and has no randomized human trial.
BPC-157: rodents and case series
TB-500: a fragment, never trialled
KPV: mouse colitis only
Narration: Lesson three moves from the cosmetic shelf to the peptides patients buy online and inject. BPC-157 is a fifteen-residue peptide first described in 1993. Its evidence is a large rodent literature, most of it from one research group, and uncontrolled human case series. TB-500 is sold as thymosin, but when anti-doping chemists analysed the product they found a sev…
units.sourceNote: Sikiric 2018 · Seiwerth 2021 · Lee 2021 · Esposito 2012 · Dalmasso 2008

assertions.text: BPC-157 is a 15-residue peptide first described in 1993.
assertions.quote: Synthetic pentadecapeptide derived from a sequence within a human gastric juice protein, first characterized by the Zagreb group (Sikiric et al.) in 1993.
assertions.note: The guide confirms BPC-157 is a synthetic 15-residue pentadecapeptide first characterized by Sikiric's group in 1993.

assertions.text: BPC-157's evidence base consists of extensive rodent literature primarily from one research group and uncontrolled human case series.
assertions.quote: Extensive rodent literature, primarily from one research group (Sikiric, Zagreb).
assertions.note: The clinical reference guide states that the evidence for BPC-157 consists of an extensive rodent literature primarily from Sikiric's group in Zagreb.

assertions.text: TB-500 is not thymosin β4, but an N-terminal acetylated 17-23 seven-residue fragment identified by analyzing the product.
assertions.quote: This work describes the detection and the identification of the N-terminal acetylated 17-23 fragment of human thymosin beta 4 (Ac-LKKTETQ) in TB-500 by means of high-performance liquid chromatography/high resolution mass spectrometry using an Orbitrap Exactive benchtop mass spectrometer.
assertions.note: Chemical analysis of TB-500 identified the 7-residue fragment (residues 17-23) of thymosin beta 4.

assertions.text: KPV is a tripeptide consisting of the C-terminal residues (11–13) of α-MSH.
assertions.quote: The aim of this study was to investigate the therapeutic potential of the melanocortin-derived tripeptide alpha-MSH(11-13) (KPV) and its mode of action in 2 models of intestinal inflammation.
assertions.note: Kannengiesser et al. describe KPV as the melanocortin-derived tripeptide alpha-MSH(11-13).

assertions.text: KPV reduces inflammation in mouse models of colitis.
assertions.quote: The melanocortin-derived tripeptide KPV showed significant anti-inflammatory effects in 2 murine models of colitis.
assertions.note: Murine colitis studies showed significant anti-inflammatory effects upon KPV administration.

assertions.text: There are no randomized human clinical trials evaluating KPV.
assertions.quote: Preclinical data for inflammatory-bowel-disease models; small open-label studies for atopic dermatitis. No randomized human trials.
assertions.note: The clinical reference notes preclinical IBD data and small open-label dermatology studies, with no randomized human trials.

units.text:
The evidence
One abstract, no published trial.
As of September 2026 no randomized efficacy trial of BPC-157 in people has been published in full. FDA's July 2026 briefing found one randomized, placebo-controlled trial reported only as a 2005 meeting abstract: 53 people with ulcerative colitis, two weeks of treatment, and no significant difference from placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov adds a 2015 phase 1 safety study that never posted results, a completed 2025 single-arm product study with no results posted, and a randomized phase 1 trial after rotator-cuff surgery due to start in 2027.
randomized efficacy trials of BPC-157 in people published in full (September 2026)
One 2005 ulcerative-colitis trial exists only as a meeting abstract (no significant difference from placebo) · registered: phase 1 safety study (2015, no results) · single-arm product study (2025, no results) · randomized phase 1…
units.sourceNote: ClinicalTrials.gov, checked 24 Sep 2026 · McGuire 2025 · Mayfield 2026

assertions.text: FDA's July 2026 briefing document identified one randomized, placebo-controlled trial of BPC-157 in ulcerative colitis reported only as a 2005 meeting abstract of 53 patients treated for two weeks with no significant difference from placebo.
assertions.quote: We identified a single meeting abstract reporting on the results of a multicenter, randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled study in subjects with UC (Ruenzi et al., 2005). A total of 53 subjects with mild to moderate (definition/inclusion criteria unclear) UC (definition and inclusion criteria unknown) were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive BPC-157 (PL 14736) enema 80 mg or placebo once daily for two weeks.
assertions.note: FDA's briefing document describes Ruenzi et al. (2005) as a 53-subject, 2-week randomized trial with no statistically significant difference versus placebo.

assertions.text: A 2015 phase 1 safety and pharmacokinetics study of BPC-157 registered on ClinicalTrials.gov never posted results.
assertions.quote: A search of Clinicaltrials.gov retrieved a single phase 1 study in healthy subjects in Mexico (NCT02637284). Subjects were to receive: 1) Phase 1a- single dose of BPC-157 (1 mg, 3 mg, or 6 mg) or placebo oral tablet by mouth and 2) Phase 1b- BPC-157 3 mg or placebo oral tablet by mouth every 8 hours for two weeks. The estimated enrollment was 42 subjects. There are no results posted, and we were unable to find an associated published study.
assertions.note: The clinical trial record and the FDA briefing document confirm no results have been posted for NCT02637284.

assertions.note: The ClinicalTrials.gov record shows an unmasked single-arm study completed in 2025 with no posted results.

units.text:
Worked example
Two trials, one peptide: LL-37.
LL-37, the skin's own cathelicidin, is the one repair peptide with two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers. Read them in order.
First trial (2014)
Positive at low dose
First-in-human, randomized, dose-ranging; 34 patients
Second trial (2021)
Negative in the full cohort
Multicentre phase IIb, placebo-controlled; only a post hoc subgroup signal
Who ran them
The developer, both times
Sponsorship does not make a trial wrong; it is one more reason to wait for replication
Grade
C — inconsistent
A small positive trial followed by an adequately powered negative one
Callout: A small positive trial is a hypothesis. LL-37 is what happens when someone tests it.
units.sourceNote: Grönberg 2014 · Mahlapuu 2021 · Schauber & Gallo 2008

assertions.text: LL-37 is the skin's endogenous cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide.
assertions.quote: Cathelicidins are unique AMPs that protect the skin through 2 distinct pathways: (1) direct antimicrobial activity and (2) initiation of a host response resulting in cytokine release, inflammation, angiogenesis, and reepithelialization.
assertions.note: The abstract confirms that cathelicidins are skin antimicrobial peptides involved in defense and repair.

assertions.text: The 2014 first-in-human trial of LL-37 was a randomized, dose-ranging study of 34 patients with hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers that was positive at low dose.
assertions.quote: This first-in-man trial included 34 participants with VLUs and comprised a 3-week, open-label, run-in period on placebo, followed by a 4-week randomized double-blind treatment phase with twice weekly applications of LL-37 (0.5, 1.6, or 3.2 mg/mL) or placebo, and a 4-week follow-up.
assertions.note: The 2014 study was a first-in-man randomized dose-ranging trial in 34 patients showing improved healing at lower doses.

assertions.text: The 2021 multicentre phase IIb trial of LL-37 was negative in the full cohort, showing only a post hoc subgroup signal.
assertions.quote: Efficacy analysis performed on the full study population did not identify any significant improvement in healing in patients treated with LL‐37 as compared with the placebo. In contrast, a post hoc analysis revealed statistically significant improvement with LL‐37 treatment in several interrelated healing parameters in the subgroup of patients with large target wounds (a wound area of at least 10 cm 2 at randomization), which is a known negative prognostic factor for healing.
assertions.note: The phase IIb trial showed no significant healing improvement in the full cohort, with an improvement seen only in a post hoc subgroup analysis of large wounds.

assertions.text: Both clinical trials of LL-37 were run/sponsored by the peptide's developer.
assertions.quote: The study was financed by Promore Pharma AB, Solna, Sweden.
assertions.note: The provided text confirms the developer sponsored the 2021 trial, but does not provide sponsorship details for the 2014 trial.

assertions.text: LL-37 is assigned Grade C evidence reflecting a small positive trial followed by an adequately powered negative one.
assertions.quote: Evidence base: two randomized placebo-controlled wound trials, the smaller positive at low dose and the larger Phase IIb negative in its full cohort with only a post hoc subgroup signal.
assertions.note: The reference guide assigns Grade C based on two trials: a smaller positive low-dose trial and a larger phase IIb trial that was negative in the full cohort.

units.text: If you practise in the UK, the route for unlicensed medicines works differently, and lesson 7.2 sets it out.

In the EU, a medicine prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formula), or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formula), falls outside Directive 2001/83/EC and needs no marketing authorisation under it (Article 3), and each member state may, under its own law, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a professional's bona fide unsolicited order, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Article 5(1)). No centrally authorised medicine containing GHK-Cu, BPC-157 or TB-500 was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026).

A 46-year-old patient has been injecting a research-use-only 'GLOW' blend bought online for three months. She reports smoother skin and asks about continuing. You notice new, patchy darkening on her face and forearms. This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence; there is one right first move.

You notice new, patchy darkening on her face and forearms. The blend has no controlled human trials, it is made outside good manufacturing practice, and the Hormonaly guide treats new pigmentation on these products as a red flag. units.text:
FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee reviewed BPC-157, KPV and TB-500 in July 2026. What does that change for 503A compounding today?
Explanation: Check the live list. A pending review is not a licence to prescribe.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): They can now be compounded, because the committee reviewed them.
Explanation: The committee advises; nothing changes until FDA adds a substance to the bulks list by rulemaking.
Correct answer: Nothing yet: the committee advises, FDA must still act by rulemaking, and until then compounded products do not qualify for the 503A exemptions.
Explanation: Correct. Review is not approval.

Advisory committees make non-binding recommendations to the FDA, which generally follows the recommendations but is not legally bound to do so.

assertions.text: The hair follicle and the cutaneous pigment system are regulated by locally produced hormones within the skin.
assertions.quote: The classical observations of the skin as a target for melanotropins have been complemented by the discovery of their actual production at the local level. In fact, all of the elements controlling the activity of the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis are expressed in the skin including CRH, urocortin, and POMC, with its products ACTH, alpha-MSH, and beta-endorphin.
assertions.note: Cutaneous production of POMC, melanotropins, ACTH, and stress-response hormones regulates local pigmentary and follicular activity.

units.text:
Mechanism
A follicle that runs its own hormones.
Human scalp hair follicles kept alive in the laboratory answer corticotropin-releasing hormone by making ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, with a feedback loop like the adrenal axis. They also run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. Locally made dihydrotestosterone shrinks genetically susceptible scalp follicles, the process behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles are shielded from immune attack, and alopecia areata begins when that shield fails.
Local stress axis: CRH → ACTH → cortisol, with feedback
Local androgen switch: testosterone → DHT in the scalp
Immune privilege: its collapse drives alopecia areata
Narration: Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do…
units.sourceNote: Ito 2005 · Horesh 2023 · Bertolini 2020 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 6

assertions.text: Human scalp hair follicles maintained in culture respond to corticotropin-releasing hormone by producing ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, operating a local HPA-like feedback loop.
assertions.quote: Thus, even in the absence of endocrine, neural, or vascular systemic connections, normal human scalp hair follicles directly respond to CRH stimulation in a strikingly similar manner to what is seen in the classical HPA axis, including synthesis and secretion of cortisol and activation of prototypic neuroendocrine feedback loops.
assertions.note: Human hair follicles in culture respond to CRH by producing POMC peptides (ACTH, α-MSH), secreting cortisol, and exhibiting negative feedback.

assertions.text: Hair follicles operate an autonomous growth hormone and IGF-1 loop.
assertions.quote: The human hair follicle runs functional peripheral equivalents of the central axes: it synthesizes cortisol and operates a local HPA-like loop,[11] and ex vivo it sustains a hypothalamic–pituitary–somatotropic equivalent (GHRH, GH, IGF-1) that paces its own growth.[12]
assertions.note: Hair follicles sustain an ex vivo equivalent of the somatotropic axis including GH and IGF-1.

assertions.text: Locally produced dihydrotestosterone (via 5-alpha-reductase conversion of testosterone) shrinks genetically susceptible scalp hair follicles in pattern hair loss.
assertions.quote: Hormones set the follicle’s tempo. Thyroid hormone and prolactin tune the cycle and estrogen withdrawal at menopause thins hair, but the dominant clinical lever is androgenic: 5α-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, which paradoxically miniaturizes genetically susceptible scalp follicles (androgenetic alopecia) while driving beard and body hair.
assertions.note: 5α-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, causing follicle miniaturization in androgenetic alopecia.

assertions.text: Growing hair follicles possess immune privilege shielding them from immune attack, and the collapse of this privilege drives alopecia areata.
assertions.quote: Collapse of anagen hair bulb IP is an essential prerequisite for the development of alopecia areata (AA).
assertions.note: Anagen hair follicles maintain immune privilege whose collapse is necessary for alopecia areata pathogenesis.

units.text:
Human evidence
Two trials, 1,200 adults, one approval.
When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A.
adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)
At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo
What it means: Interrupting the immune signalling behind collapsed privilege regrows hair in severe alopecia areata. That is approval-grade evidence (A), and it shows what real follicle evidence looks like.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about pattern hair loss, cosmetic thinning or any pe…
units.sourceNote: King 2022 (BRAVE-AA1 and -AA2) · FDA approval letter, 13 Jun 2022

assertions.text: Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata.
assertions.quote: We enrolled 654 patients in the BRAVE-AA1 trial and 546 in the BRAVE-AA2 trial.
assertions.note: The BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 phase 3 trials enrolled a combined 1,200 adult patients with severe alopecia areata.

assertions.quote: It is also an immune-privileged site — normally shielded from immune attack — and collapse of that privilege drives alopecia areata, now treatable with JAK inhibitors that interrupt the responsible cytokine signaling (oral baricitinib is approved for severe disease GRADE A).[13]
assertions.note: The pocket guide explicitly gives baricitinib for severe alopecia areata a Grade A evidence rating.

assertions.text: At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib achieved a SALT score of 20 or less (at least 80% scalp hair coverage), compared to 3–6% on placebo.
assertions.quote: The estimated percentage of patients with a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36 was 38.8% with 4-mg baricitinib, 22.8% with 2-mg baricitinib, and 6.2% with placebo in BRAVE-AA1 and 35.9%, 19.4%, and 3.3%, respectively, in BRAVE-AA2.
assertions.note: At week 36, 38.8% of patients receiving 4-mg baricitinib in BRAVE-AA1 (and 35.9% in BRAVE-AA2) achieved a SALT score <= 20, compared with 6.2% and 3.3% on placebo.

assertions.text: Both phase 3 trials of baricitinib were funded by the manufacturer, and the study authors stated that longer trials are required.
assertions.quote: Longer trials are required to assess the efficacy and safety of baricitinib for alopecia areata. (Funded by Eli Lilly under license from Incyte; BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT03570749 and NCT03899259.).
assertions.note: The trials were funded by Eli Lilly and the authors concluded that longer trials are needed.

What changes in practice
Work up the hair loss before anyone mentions a peptide.
Pattern, trigger, patches and androgens decide the treatment. Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men. Approved options exist, with A-grade evidence
Severe or fast-spreading alopecia areata goes to dermatology

A 32-year-old woman asks for a compounded peptide scalp spray. Diffuse shedding began three months after she gave birth; there are no patches and no signs of androgen excess. What comes first?

units.text:
Lesson 5.2 · Concept
Five receptors, one family of hormones.
Skin makes proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cuts it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors. MC1R drives pigment in skin and hair, MC2R answers ACTH in the adrenal gland, MC3R and MC4R act in the brain on appetite, and MC5R governs sebum. Which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.
MC1R: pigment of skin and hair
MC2R: adrenal · MC5R: sebum
MC3R and MC4R: appetite, in the brain
Narration: Pigment starts with hormones the skin makes for itself. Skin cells produce a precursor called POMC and cut it into ACTH, alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. There are five melanocortin receptors. MC1R sets the pigment of skin and hair. MC2R is the adrenal receptor for ACTH. MC3R and …
units.sourceNote: Slominski & Wortsman 2000 · Laiho & Murray 2022 · Böhm 2025

units.text:
Four registers
One receptor family, two very different molecules.
Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH. Compare them register by register and the resemblance ends at the receptor.
Mechanism
Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist · Melanotan II: non-selective
Melanotan II also acts on MC3R, MC4R and MC5R and reaches the brain
Human evidence
Afamelanotide: A, for EPP only · Melanotan II: D
Two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, against a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s. The Peptide Pocket Guide rates Melanotan II C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D; with no trial of tanning, this course uses D.
Regulatory status
Afamelanotide: EU 2014, US 2019 · Melanotan II: none
Afamelanotide is approved only for EPP, as the manufacturer's implant. Melanotan II is approved for no indication anywhere.
Ope…

units.text:
The evidence
Sixty-nine hours against forty-one.
Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.
69 vs 41 h
median pain-free hours in direct sunlight over six months, afamelanotide vs placebo (US phase 3 trial, 94 adults with EPP)
Langendonk et al., NEJM 2015 · European trial, 74 adults: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months
What it means: Afamelanotide lets people with EPP spend more time in sunlight without pain. That is approval-grade evidence (A) for one rare disease.
What it does not mean: It says nothing about cosmetic tanning, about Melanotan II, or about …
units.sourceNote: Langendonk 2015 (NEJM) · FDA Scenesse label, Aug 2024 · EMA EPAR

assertions.text: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain.
assertions.quote: Erythropoietic protoporphyria is a severe photodermatosis that is associated with acute phototoxicity. Patients with this condition have excruciating pain and a markedly reduced quality of life.
assertions.note: The NEJM paper describes EPP as a rare disorder causing acute phototoxicity and severe painful photosensitivity.

assertions.text: In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, compared to 40.8 hours on placebo.
assertions.quote: In the U.S. study, the duration of pain-free time after 6 months was longer in the afamelanotide group (median, 69.4 hours, vs. 40.8 hours in the placebo group; P = 0.04).
assertions.note: The phase 3 results reported in NEJM confirm these exact median pain-free sunlight exposure durations over 6 months.

assertions.text: The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions with afamelanotide.
assertions.quote: In the European Union study, the duration of pain-free time after 9 months was also longer in the afamelanotide group than in the placebo group (median, 6.0 hours vs. 0.8 hours; P = 0.005), and the number of phototoxic reactions was lower in the the afamelanotide group (77 vs. 146, P = 0.04).
assertions.note: The European trial showed significantly longer pain-free time and significantly fewer phototoxic reactions in the afamelanotide group.

assertions.text: Both phase 3 trials of afamelanotide in EPP were funded by the manufacturer.
assertions.quote: The study was designed and sponsored by Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals, with input from investigators in the European Union and the United States.
assertions.note: The study publication notes funding and sponsorship by the drug's manufacturer, Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals.

assertions.text: The US trial included 94 adults and the European trial included 74 adults (where median pain-free hours over 9 months were 6.0 vs 0.8 hours).
assertions.quote: Patients in the European Union (74 patients) and the United States (94 patients) were randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, to receive a subcutaneous implant containing either afamelanotide or placebo every 60 days (a total of five implants in the European Union study and three in the U.S study).
assertions.note: The participant counts and European trial primary endpoint median values match the trial publication.

units.text:
Safety signals
What the case reports show.
The harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews, so they show what can happen without telling you how often. Reported skin effects include darkening and growth of existing moles, crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi, and dark bands in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use, each in someone with other risk factors, so causation is unproven. Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism needing surgery and a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis, and FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.
Skin: changing moles, eruptive naevi, melanonychia
Melanoma: reported, causation unproven
Systemic: priapism, rhabdomyolysis, encephalopathy
Narration: Now the harms, and the kind of evidence behind them. Everything here comes from case reports and revie…

assertions.note: A case report confirms new eruptive atypical naevi and darkening/growth of preexisting moles following use of synthetic alpha-MSH.

New moles after a summer of tanning shots.

This is a fictional case built from the lesson's evidence, and one move clearly comes before the others.

Family history of melanoma: the guide's absolute contraindication

Three regulators, one answer.

units.text:
A patient says, 'Afamelanotide is approved, so Melanotan II is basically the same drug.' What is the accurate reply?
Explanation: Name the molecule, then its indication: approval does not transfer between them.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Yes. They act on the same receptor, so the approval covers both.
Explanation: Sharing MC1R does not make them the same molecule, and an approval attaches to one product and one indication.
Correct answer: They are different molecules. Afamelanotide is approved only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II acts on several receptors, is approved nowhere, and is linked in case reports to changing moles and priapism.
Explanation: Correct. Same family, different selectivity, different evidence and different legal standing.
Distractor (deliberately false, not a claim): Melanotan II is safe if it comes from a reputable seller.
Explanat…

units.text:
Lesson 5.3 · Concept
A Wnt switch and a zinc question.
PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating peptide to a short decoy sequence that stops the protein CXXC5 from binding Dishevelled. Freed from that brake, Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises, and in mice hair regrew faster. Its developers also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp. Zinc thymulin is a thymic peptide that is active only when bound to zinc. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.
PTD-DBM: releases a Wnt brake (mouse data)
Zinc thymulin: a zinc-dependent thymic peptide
Both: mechanism first, human data absent
Narration: Two peptides are sold for hair, and both arrive with better stories than data. PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment borrowed from an HIV protein to a short decoy sequence. Inside follicle cells, the decoy keeps a protein called …
units.sourceNote: Lee 2017 (J Invest Dermatol) · Dardenne 1982 · Peptide Pocket Guide

assertions.text: PTD-DBM is a peptide therapy that competes with CXXC5 to prevent it from binding Dishevelled (Dvl).
assertions.quote: For example, PTD-DBM is a peptide therapy that competes with CXXC5 for binding with Dvl [ 21 ].
assertions.note: Mehta 2025 explains that PTD-DBM competes with CXXC5 for Dishevelled binding.

assertions.text: Disrupting the CXXC5-Dishevelled interaction activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and accelerates hair regrowth and wound-induced hair follicle neogenesis in mice.
assertions.quote: Disrupting the CXXC5-Dishevelled interaction with a competitor peptide activated the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and accelerated hair regrowth and wound-induced hair follicle neogenesis.
assertions.note: Lee 2017 reports that competitor peptide disruption of CXXC5-Dishevelled activated Wnt/β-catenin and accelerated hair regrowth and follicle neogenesis.

assertions.text: CXXC5 expression is upregulated in miniaturized hair follicles in human balding scalps.
assertions.quote: CXXC5 was upregulated in miniaturized hair follicles and arrector pili muscles in human balding scalps.
assertions.note: Lee 2017 found CXXC5 upregulated in miniaturized follicles in human balding scalp.

assertions.text: Thymulin is biologically active only when bound to zinc.
assertions.quote: These data indicate the existence of two forms of FTS. The first one lacks Zn and is biologically inactive; the second one contains Zn and is biologically active, for which we propose the name of "thymulin" (FTS-Zn).
assertions.note: Dardenne 1982 demonstrated that the zinc-lacking form is inactive, while the zinc-bound form (thymulin) is biologically active.

assertions.text: The mechanism of zinc thymulin in hair growth is undefined, and whether any effect comes from the peptide or from zinc is unknown.
assertions.quote: The role of the zinc cofactor itself complicates the question of whether 'zinc thymulin' acts as a peptide or as a vehicle for topical zinc.
assertions.note: The clinical reference notes that it remains unclear whether zinc thymulin acts as a peptide or simply as a vehicle for zinc delivery.

units.text:
The evidence
Zero trials in people.
As of September 2026, PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov list no human trial of PTD-DBM, published or registered. Its evidence is one 2017 study in mice and human scalp tissue from the developer's group, whose senior author is affiliated with a biotech company. A 2025 review's summary speaks of 'clinical efficacy', yet the review's own text describes PTD-DBM results in mouse models only.
human trials of PTD-DBM, published or registered (September 2026)
Lee et al., J Invest Dermatol 2017: mice, plus CXXC5 measured in human scalp tissue
What it means: Whether PTD-DBM regrows human hair is unknown. The Peptide Pocket Guide and this course grade it D.
What it does not mean: It does not show that PTD-DBM fails or harms. One open safety question sits alongside: the 2025 review flags that off-target Wnt activation is associated with colorectal and liver cancers, a…

assertions.text: The 2017 study by Lee et al. evaluated PTD-DBM / CXXC5 in mice and human scalp tissue.
assertions.quote: CXXC5 was upregulated in miniaturized hair follicles and arrector pili muscles in human balding scalps. The inhibitory effects of CXXC5 on alkaline phosphatase activity and cell proliferation were demonstrated using human hair follicle dermal papilla cells. Moreover, CXXC5 -/- mice displayed accelerated hair regrowth, and treatment with valproic acid, a glycogen synthase kinase 3β inhibitor that activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, further induced hair regrowth in the CXXC5 -/- mice.
assertions.note: Lee et al. demonstrated CXXC5 upregulation in human balding scalps and tested the competing peptide / CXXC5-knockout in mice.

units.text:
Lesson 6.1 · Mechanism
Two hormones, two layers of skin.
Growth hormone acts mostly in the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more by fibroblasts than by keratinocytes, and it increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis. IGF-1, made locally by fibroblasts and melanocytes, reaches keratinocytes through the IGF-1 receptor and makes them divide. Human hair follicles even run their own small growth-hormone loop in the laboratory. With age, GH secretion and IGF-1 fall steadily; this is the somatopause.
GH: dermal fibroblasts and collagen
IGF-1: keratinocyte proliferation, supplied locally
Somatopause: GH and IGF-1 fall with age
Narration: Two layers of skin listen to two different parts of the same axis. Growth hormone speaks mainly to the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more on fibroblasts than on keratinocytes, and in culture growth hormone increases fibroblast numbers and…

assertions.text: The growth hormone receptor is expressed at higher levels in dermal fibroblasts than in keratinocytes.
assertions.quote: Northern analysis, using the cloned GH-R as probe, revealed relatively higher levels of GH-R transcripts in cultured human dermal fibroblasts compared to cultured keratinocytes or keratome biopsies.
assertions.note: Northern analysis demonstrated higher levels of GH receptor transcripts in cultured dermal fibroblasts than in keratinocytes.

assertions.text: Growth hormone increases fibroblast cell numbers and supports dermal collagen synthesis.
assertions.quote: GH activity, sometimes mediated via IGF-I, is primarily evident in the dermis, particularly affecting collagen synthesis.
assertions.note: Edmondson et al. state that GH activity is primarily evident in the dermis, particularly affecting collagen synthesis.

assertions.text: IGF-1 is produced locally by dermal fibroblasts and melanocytes, while keratinocytes express the IGF-1 receptor.
assertions.quote: mRNA transcripts for the major mediator of GH actions, insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), were detected by PCR in fibroblasts, melanocytes, and keratome biopsies, but not in keratinocytes. In contrast, IGF-1 receptor mRNA were abundant in cultured keratinocytes and skin biopsies, as determined by Northern analysis.
assertions.note: Tavakkol et al. detected IGF-1 transcripts in fibroblasts and melanocytes but not keratinocytes, whereas IGF-1 receptor mRNA was abundant in keratinocytes.

assertions.text: Human hair follicles maintain an autonomous somatotropic loop ex vivo.
assertions.quote: The human hair follicle runs functional peripheral equivalents of the central axes: it synthesizes cortisol and operates a local HPA-like loop,[11] and ex vivo it sustains a hypothalamic–pituitary–somatotropic equivalent (GHRH, GH, IGF-1) that paces its own growth.[12]

assertions.text: Growth hormone secretion declines with age, a change referred to as the somatopause.
assertions.quote: Each axis has its own clock: somatopause and adrenopause are steep and early; andropause is gradual; menopause is abrupt.
assertions.note: Chapter 2 notes the age-related somatopause decline in the growth-hormone axis.

units.text:
Human evidence
A much-cited skin result, read again.
In 1990 a much-cited New England Journal of Medicine study gave growth hormone for six months to 12 healthy men over 60, with nine untreated men for comparison and no placebo. Lean mass rose and fat fell. Skin thickness rose 7.1%, with P = 0.07, short of statistical significance. A small 1996 randomized trial in 28 older men found 15% more collagen laid down in implanted wound tubes on GH, a laboratory surrogate for repair.

P = 0.07 · nine untreated men as comparison · no placebo

What it does not mean: It does not show that GH thins skin or that it fails in true deficiency, and it…

units.text:
What changes in practice
Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.
In healthy older adults, randomized trials of growth hormone show small shifts in body composition, about 2 kg less fat and 2 kg more lean mass, with more oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and a trend towards diabetes. Strength and endurance change little. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades its advice against treatment A; graded on the trials themselves the evidence is B, and the conclusion is the same. In the US, as of September 2026, knowingly distributing growth hormone for anti-ageing is a federal offence.
Healthy ageing: small body-composition change, more side-effects
Grade B on the trials (guide: A), same conclusion
US: anti-ageing distribution is a federal offence

assertions.text: In healthy older adults, randomized trials of growth hormone show body-composition changes of approximately 2 kg reduction in fat mass and 2 kg increase in lean mass.

assertions.note: A meta-analysis of trials in healthy older adults found a 2.1 kg decrease in fat mass and a 2.1 kg increase in lean body mass.

assertions.text: In healthy older adults, growth hormone trials show higher rates of oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome, and a trend towards impaired fasting glucose or diabetes.
assertions.quote: Persons treated with GH were significantly more likely to experience soft tissue edema, arthralgias, carpal tunnel syndrome, and gynecomastia and were somewhat more likely to experience the onset of diabetes mellitus and impaired fasting glucose.
assertions.note: Randomized trials report significantly higher incidence of soft-tissue edema, arthralgias, carpal tunnel syndrome, and increased rates of impaired glucose tolerance/diabetes.

assertions.text: In healthy older adults receiving growth hormone alone, muscle strength and endurance change little.
assertions.quote: Women's strength decreased in the placebo group and increased nonsignificantly with HRT (P =.09), GH (P =.29), and GH + HRT (P =.14). Men's strength also did not increase significantly except for a marginally significant increase of 13.5 kg with GH + testosterone (P =.05).

assertions.note: The clinical pocket guide rates its recommendation against growth hormone in healthy older adults as Grade A.

assertions.text: In the United States, knowingly distributing growth hormone for anti-ageing or non-authorized medical conditions is a federal criminal offence.

units.text:
Lesson 6.2 · Concept
One axis, four ways in.
Somatropin is growth hormone itself. GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary's GHRH receptor. Ghrelin-receptor agonists (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral ibutamoren, MK-677) stimulate GH release through a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary altogether. They are sold as one family, and the next moments take them apart.
Replace: somatropin
Stimulate: GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists
Bypass: IGF-1 analogues
Narration: Four routes lead into the same axis, and patients rarely know which one they are on. Somatropin is growth hormone itself, made by recombinant technology. GHRH analogues, sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, press on the pituitary's releasing-hormone receptor, so the gland releases its own growth hormone in pulses. Ghrelin-receptor ag…
units.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 3 · Peptide Pocket Guide, growth-hormone axis · Dominikowski 2026

assertions.text: Somatropin is human growth hormone produced by recombinant technology.
assertions.quote: Somatropin is a human growth hormone produced by recombinant DNA technology in Escherichia coli. The protein is comprised of 191 amino acid residues and has a molecular weight of 22,124 daltons.
assertions.note: The prescribing information confirms somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone.

assertions.text: GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, and CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary GHRH receptor to promote endogenous pulsatile growth hormone release.
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing hormone (GHRH) analogues are synthetic peptides designed to stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the pituitary GHRH receptor, thereby increasing GH pulsatility and secondarily IGF-1. Because they act upstream of GH release, their effects remain largely shaped by physiological regulatory loops
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 confirms that GHRH analogues like sermorelin, tesamorelin, and CJC-1295 stimulate endogenous GH pulsatility via the pituitary GHRH receptor.

assertions.text: Ghrelin-receptor agonists (including ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, and oral MK-677/ibutamoren) stimulate GH release via a second pituitary receptor (GHSR-1a).
assertions.quote: Growth hormone–releasing peptides (GHRPs) are short synthetic peptides that stimulate endogenous GH secretion by activating the ghrelin receptor - the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHSR-1a), at the level of the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary.
assertions.note: Dominikowski 2026 describes how GHRPs act as agonists at the pituitary ghrelin receptor (GHSR-1a) to induce GH secretion.

assertions.text: IGF-1 analogues like IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary and act directly on the IGF-1 receptor.
assertions.quote: Binds IGF-1R (a receptor tyrosine kinase), driving PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MAPK/ERK signaling — muscle protein synthesis, satellite-cell activation, glucose uptake, nitrogen retention, proliferation, and fat oxidation — independently of growth hormone.
assertions.note: The Peptide Pocket Guide confirms IGF-1 LR3 acts directly on the IGF-1 receptor independently of growth hormone.

units.text:
Worked example
What real peptide evidence looks like.
Tesamorelin is the instructive exception on this axis. Both Hormonaly guides grade it A, for one indication. Read the record in order.
Trials
Two phase 3 RCTs, 806 patients
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled and run by the developer, in adults with HIV and excess abdominal fat
Result
About 15% less visceral fat than placebo at 26 weeks
Subcutaneous fat unchanged; the reduction held to 52 weeks on continued treatment
US status (label, August 2026)
FDA-approved since 2010, for one use
Reduction of excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. The label says it is not for weight loss and that long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established.
Safety, in its own label
IGF-1 above +2 SD in 47% at 26 weeks
Diabetes-range HbA1c in 5% against 1% on placebo; fluid retention; contraindicated in active malign…
units.sourceNote: Falutz 2007, 2010 · EGRIFTA WR prescribing information (DailyMed, August 2026) · MHRA Products database (searched 25 Sep 2026)

assertions.text: Tesamorelin was evaluated in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 clinical trials pooling 806 adult patients with HIV and excess abdominal fat.
assertions.quote: A total of 806 ART-treated HIV patients with excess abdominal fat were randomized in a 2:1 fashion to receive tesamorelin 2 mg (n = 543) or placebo (n = 263) sc daily.
assertions.note: Falutz 2010 pooled two phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials comprising 806 HIV patients with excess abdominal fat.

assertions.text: Tesamorelin reduced visceral adipose tissue by approximately 15% compared to placebo at 26 weeks.
assertions.quote: At wk 26, VAT decreased significantly in tesamorelin-treated patients (-24 +/- 41 vs. 2 +/- 35 cm(2), tesamorelin vs. placebo, P < 0.001; treatment effect, -15.4%).
assertions.note: The pooled phase 3 trial reported a -15.4% treatment effect on visceral adipose tissue at 26 weeks.

assertions.text: In the phase 3 trials, subcutaneous fat was unchanged and the reduction in visceral fat was maintained up to 52 weeks with continued tesamorelin treatment.
assertions.quote: Treatment with tesamorelin reduces VAT and maintains the reduction for up to 52 wk, preserves abdominal sc adipose tissue, improves body image and lipids, and is overall well tolerated without clinically meaningful changes in glucose parameters.
assertions.note: Subcutaneous fat had no significant change and VAT reduction was maintained to 52 weeks in the T-T group.

assertions.text: Tesamorelin has been FDA-approved since 2010 specifically for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adult patients with lipodystrophy, with labeling stating it is not for weight loss management and that long-term cardiovascular safety is not established.
assertions.quote: EGRIFTA WR is indicated for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adult patients with lipodystrophy. Limitations of Use: Long-term cardiovascular safety of EGRIFTA WR has not been established. Consider risk/benefit of continuation of treatment in patients who have not had a reduction in visceral adipose tissue. EGRIFTA WR is not indicated for weight loss management as it has a weight neutral effect.
assertions.note: The FDA label confirms initial approval in 2010 for this indication and lists these exact limitations of use.

assertions.text: At 26 weeks of treatment, 47% of patients receiving tesamorelin had IGF-1 levels exceeding 2 standard deviation scores.
assertions.quote: Among patients who received EGRIFTA for 26 weeks, 47% had IGF-1 levels greater than 2 standard deviation scores (SDS), and 36% had SDS >3, with this effect seen as early as 13 weeks of treatment.
assertions.note: The FDA prescribing information confirms that 47% of patients at 26 weeks had IGF-1 SDS > 2.

assertions.text: In clinical trials, diabetes-range HbA1c (≥6.5%) occurred in 5% of tesamorelin-treated patients versus 1% on placebo, fluid retention can occur, and active malignancy is a contraindication.
assertions.quote: During clinical trials, the percentages of patients with elevated HbA 1c  (≥ 6.5%) from baseline to Week 26 were 5% and 1% in the EGRIFTA and placebo groups, respectively.
assertions.note: The prescribing information confirms 5% vs 1% with HbA1c >= 6.5%, notes fluid retention risks, and lists active malignancy under contraindications.

units.text:
The evidence
Zero skin trials.
A PubMed search in September 2026 found no randomized trial with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3. The nearest is a 1997 study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue related to sermorelin, in 19 older adults. Skin thickness measured by caliper rose after 16 weeks, compared with a placebo lead-in rather than a parallel control group.
randomized trials with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3 (PubMed, September 2026)
Closest: a 1997 single-blind study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue, 19 older adults, skin thickness by caliper
What it means: Every skin promise made for these peptides rests on mechanism and anecdote. The nearest data are one small study without a parallel control group (D).
What it does not mean: It does not show these peptides harm skin or do nothing for it. It shows the question has never been properl…

assertions.text: Tesamorelin has approval-grade clinical trials supporting its use for HIV-associated abdominal fat.
assertions.quote: Tesamorelin is the most comprehensively characterised GHRH analogue from a regulatory and clinical-trial perspective, supported by an FDA-approved indication and a comparatively substantial randomised clinical trial evidence base in HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
assertions.note: Tesamorelin is supported by randomized trials and FDA approval for HIV-associated lipodystrophy.

assertions.text: Somatropin has approval-grade clinical trials supporting its use for adult growth hormone deficiency.
assertions.quote: In adults with GHD, treatment with GENOTROPIN results in reduced fat mass, increased lean body mass, metabolic alterations that include beneficial changes in lipid metabolism, and normalization of IGF-I concentrations.
assertions.note: Prescribing information details regulatory approval and clinical trial efficacy for adult growth hormone deficiency.

assertions.text: Sermorelin raises hormone levels (GH/IGF-1) but lacks RCT evidence of clinical benefit for youthful GH in healthy adults.

assertions.text: CJC-1295 with DAC raises hormone levels (GH and IGF-1) but has no controlled trials demonstrating clinical benefits on skin or recovery.
assertions.quote: Phase I PK/PD studies in healthy adults; no controlled efficacy data ( 80 , 122 ).
assertions.note: Phase I trials demonstrate sustained increases in GH and IGF-1, but no controlled efficacy trials exist.

assertions.text: CJC-1295 without DAC has no published human studies.
assertions.quote: By contrast, “CJC-1295 without DAC” remains essentially uncharacterised in the peer-reviewed human literature. To date, no controlled clinical studies have directly evaluated this compound in humans, and assertions regarding physiologic GH pulsatility or improvements in body composition derive largely from extrapolation from related compounds (primarily GHRH(1–29), known as sermorelin, as previously described), as well as from non-academic sources, rather than from direct clinical evidence ( 81 ).
assertions.note: The review notes that no controlled clinical studies have directly evaluated CJC-1295 without DAC in humans.

assertions.text: Ipamorelin raises GH levels in phase I studies but has no demonstrated efficacy or benefit for anti-ageing.
assertions.quote: Phase I human studies and postoperative-ileus clinical development; no efficacy data in GH-related metabolic indications ( 103 – 105 ).
assertions.note: Phase I data confirm GH release, but there are no efficacy data in GH-related metabolic or anti-aging indications.

assertions.text: IGF-1 LR3 has no published peer-reviewed human clinical studies.
assertions.quote: The evidentiary basis differs by an order of magnitude across the compounds reviewed, ranging from regulatory-grade RCT data (tesamorelin, tier A), through phase I/II human studies without controlled efficacy data for performance-related endpoints (most GHRH analogues and ghrelin-mimetic secretagogues, tier B), to compounds with only limited or indirect human data (AOD9604, tier B/C), and finally to compounds for which no peer-reviewed human studies exist at all (CJC-1295 without DAC, PEG-MGF, IGF-1 LR3, tier D).
assertions.note: The evidence review places IGF-1 LR3 in tier D with no peer-reviewed human studies published.

Name the indication before the molecule.

Lesson 6.3 · Recognition
What too much growth hormone looks like.
Sustained GH excess changes skin in ways you can see. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema make the face, hands and feet puffy and thick; the skin turns oily with large pores; sweating increases; skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. Drugs on this axis bring their own signs: fluid retention with swelling, joint pain, tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. The Endocrine Society recommends measuring IGF-1 when typical acral and facial features are present.
Soft tissue: puffy, thickened face, hands and feet
Skin: oily, sweaty, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans
On treatment: swelling, joint pain, tingling
Narration: Excess growth hormone leaves visible marks on skin and soft tissue, and noticing them early matters. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken the face, hands and feet, so featur…
